God Most High says: ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that: gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He will give you palaces.﴾ ﴿But they denied the Hour, and We have prepared a blazing Fire for those who deny the Hour.﴾ ﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they hear its raging and roaring.﴾ ﴿And when they are cast into a narrow place of it, bound together, they will cry out for destruction there.﴾ ﴿Do not cry out for one destruction today, but cry out for many destructions.﴾

Know that this is the second answer to that doubt. His words ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that﴾ mean: better than what they mentioned of worldly blessings, such as the treasure and the garden. He explained that "better" with His words ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He will give you palaces﴾. By this, He, glorified be He, draws attention to the fact that He is able to give the Messenger everything they mentioned. However, He Most High manages His servants according to what is beneficial, or according to the requirements of His will, and no one may object to Him regarding any of His actions. So He opens to one person the doors of knowledge and wisdom and closes to him the doors of worldly things, and it is the reverse for another. This is only because He does what He wills. Here there are several issues:

The first issue: Ibn Abbas said: "Better than that" means better than what they reproached you for lacking, which is the garden, because they reproached you for lacking a single garden, while He, glorified be He, is able to give you many gardens. In the narration of Ikrimah, He said: ﴿better than that﴾, meaning better than walking in the markets and seeking livelihood.

The second issue: His words ﴿if He wills﴾ mean that He, glorified be He, is able to do that, not that He Most High is in doubt, because doubt is not permissible concerning God Most High. Some people said: "If" here means "when," that is, We have already granted you gardens in the Hereafter and built palaces for you. He placed "if" only to alert the servants that one does not attain that except by His mercy, that it is contingent upon His pure will, and that no servant has any right over God, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter.

The third issue: "Qusur" is the plural of "qasr," which is an elevated dwelling. It is possible that each garden has a palace, so that it is both a dwelling and a place of recreation. It is also permissible that the palaces are plural and the gardens are plural. Mujahid said: "If He wills, He will give you gardens in the Hereafter and palaces in this world."

The fourth issue: Al-Farra' differed concerning His words ﴿and He will give﴾. Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim raised the lam (making it a nominative form, [wa-yaj'alu]), while others made it jussive. Whoever made it jussive means: if He wills, He will give you gardens and He will give you palaces. Whoever raised it means that it is a new sentence, and the meaning is: He will surely give you palaces. This is the view of al-Zajjaj. Al-Wahidi said: There is a difference in meaning between the two readings. According to the jussive reading, the meaning is: if He wills, He will give you palaces in this world, and it is not good to stop at "the rivers." According to the raised reading, it is good to stop at "the rivers" and begin anew, meaning: and He will give you palaces in the Hereafter. In the codex of Ubayy and Ibn Mas'ud it reads: "Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give."

The fifth issue: From Tawus, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "While the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was sitting, with Jibril (peace be upon him) beside him, Jibril (peace be upon him) said: This is an angel who has descended from the heavens, having asked his Lord for permission to visit you. He did not wait long before the angel came, greeted the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and said: 'God gives you the choice between being given the keys of everything that was not given to anyone before you and will not be given to anyone after you, without it diminishing for you anything of what He has stored up for you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Rather, let Him gather them all for me in the Hereafter.' Then the words ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills﴾ were revealed, to the end of the verse." And from Ibn Abbas, who said, peace be upon him: "Jibril offered me the gold of the valley of Mecca [Batha' Makkah], [page 48] and I said: 'Rather, a satisfied night and three hungry days,' and that is more for my remembrance and my request to my Lord." In the narration of Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Abd al-Wahhab, he (peace be upon him) said: "I eat my fill one day and go hungry three days; I praise You when I am satisfied, and I humble myself before You when I am hungry." And from al-Dahhak: "When the polytheists reproached the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for poverty, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) grieved over that. Then Jibril (peace be upon him) descended, consoling him, and said: 'God sends you His greetings and says: ﴿We did not send any messengers before you except that they ate food﴾ [al-Furqan: 20], to the end of the verse.'" He said: "While Jibril (peace be upon him) and the Prophet (ﷺ) were talking, a door of the gates of heaven opened that had not been opened before. Then he said: 'Rejoice, O Muhammad, this is Ridwan, keeper of the Garden. He has come to you with approval from your Lord.' So he greeted him and said: 'Your Lord gives you the choice between being a prophet-king and being a prophet-servant.' With him was a casket of light, shining. Then he said: 'These are the keys to the treasuries of this world; take them without God diminishing for you anything of what He has prepared for you in the Hereafter, not even the wing of a gnat.' The Prophet (ﷺ) looked at Jibril as one seeking counsel, and he gestured with his hand, meaning: humble yourself. So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'Rather, a prophet-servant.'" He said: After that, he (peace be upon him) never ate reclining until he departed this world.

* * *

As for God Most High's words ﴿But they denied the Hour, and We have prepared a blazing Fire for those who deny the Hour﴾, this is a third answer to that doubt. It is as if He, glorified be He, said: What they have clung to is not a doubt against you in itself; rather, what led them to deny you is their denial of the Hour, out of their reluctance to prepare for it. It is also possible that the meaning is that they deny the Hour, so they do not hope for reward or fear punishment, and they do not bear the burden of reflection and thought. Therefore they do not benefit from the proofs presented to them. Then He said: ﴿And We have prepared a blazing Fire for those who deny the Hour﴾. Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: Abu Muslim said: "And We have prepared" means: We made it ready and prepared for them. "Sa'ir" is a fierce fire of great blaze. From al-Hasan: it is one of the names of Jahannam (Hell).

The second issue: Our companions [the Ash'aris] argued that Paradise is created from His words ﴿It has been prepared for the God-fearing﴾ [Al 'Imran: 133], and that the Fire, which is the abode of punishment, is created from this verse, namely His words ﴿And We have prepared a blazing Fire for those who deny the Hour﴾. His words ﴿And We have prepared﴾ are a report of an act that occurred in the past, so the verse indicates that the abode of punishment is created. Al-Jubba'i said: "We have prepared" may mean the Fire in this world, with which God punishes the unbelievers and the wicked in their graves; and it may mean the Fire of the Hereafter, and the meaning of "We have prepared" would be: We will prepare it for them, as in His words: ﴿And the companions of the Garden will call out to the companions of the Fire﴾ [al-A'raf: 44]. Know that this objection is extremely weak, because what is meant by "sa'ir" is either the fire of this world or the fire of the Hereafter. If it is the first, then either the meaning is that He punishes them in this world with the fire of this world, or He punishes them in the Hereafter with the fire of this world. The first is false, because He did not punish them with fire in this world. The second is also false, because none of the community has said that God punishes the disbelievers in the Hereafter with the fires of this world. Therefore it is established that what is meant is the Fire of the Hereafter, and it is established that it is prepared. To interpret the verse as meaning that God will make it prepared is to abandon the apparent meaning without evidence. And since al-Hasan said that "sa'ir" is one of the names of Jahannam, His words ﴿And We have prepared a blazing Fire for those who deny the Hour﴾ are explicit that God has prepared Hell.

The third issue: Our companions argued by this verse that the one who is happy (sa'id) is the one who was made happy in his mother's womb. They said: Those for whom God has prepared the blazing Fire, and whom He reported and decreed for that, if they became believers among the people of reward, then God's judgment that they are among the people of the Fire would have become false, and His knowledge would have become ignorance. This reversal is impossible, and whatever leads to the impossible is impossible. Therefore, the transformation of those people into believers among the people of reward is impossible. It is thus established that the happy one does not become wretched, and the wretched one does not become happy.

* * *

Then, glorified and exalted be He, described the blazing Fire with attributes:

[Page 49] The first of them is His words: ﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they hear its raging and roaring.﴾ Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: "Sa'ir" is masculine, but here it appears feminine, because He said ﴿saw them﴾ and ﴿they heard for it﴾. It came feminine according to the meaning of "fire" (nar).

The second issue: The doctrine of our companions is that life is not conditional upon bodily structure. Thus the fire, in its present state, may have life, reason and speech created in it by God. For the Mu'tazilah (the rationalist school), this is not permissible. These Mu'tazilah have no proof in this matter except the extrapolation from habitual experience. Even if that were true, it would necessitate denying the breaking of habits in the case of the messengers. So their position is self-contradictory. Rather, rejecting habits befits only the principles of the philosophers. Accordingly, our companions said: God's words describing the Fire, ﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they hear its raging and roaring﴾, must be taken in their apparent sense, because there is no impossibility in the Fire being living, seeing, and enraged against the disbelievers. As for the Mu'tazilah, they had to resort to interpretation, and they mentioned several ways of doing so:

One of them: They said: "It sees them" means "it appears to them," from the expression "their houses are in view of each other" (tatarra'a), meaning they face each other. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "The fires of a believer and an unbeliever do not see each other," meaning they do not face each other, because the believer is obliged to keep away from the unbeliever and the polytheist. It is said: "The houses of so-and-so are facing," meaning they are opposite each other.

The second: The Fire, because of the intensity of its blazing and boiling, becomes as if it sees the unbelievers, seeks them out, and rages against them.

The third: Al-Jubba'i said: God mentioned the Fire but meant the guardians entrusted with punishing the people of the Fire, because seeing is possible for them but not for the Fire. It is like His words ﴿and ask the town﴾ [Yusuf: 82], meaning its people.

The third issue: One may say: Raging is an expression for intense anger, and that cannot be heard. How then did God say ﴿they heard for it raging and roaring﴾? The answer to this has several aspects:

The first: Although raging cannot be heard, what indicates it may be heard, namely a sound. It is like saying: "I saw the anger of the commander against so-and-so," when one sees what indicates it. The same is said about love. So here too: they heard for it a sound resembling the sound of one who rages. This is the view of al-Zajjaj.

The second: The meaning is: they knew of its raging and heard its roaring. This is the view of Qutrub, and it is like the words of the poet:

Girding a sword and a spear.

The third: What is meant is the raging of the guardians.

The fourth issue: Ubayd ibn Umayr said: Jahannam emits a roar such that no one remains without his limbs trembling, until Ibrahim (peace be upon him) falls on his knees saying: "Myself, myself!"

* * *

The second attribute of the Fire: God Most High's words ﴿And when they are cast into a narrow place of it, bound together, they will cry out for destruction there.﴾ Know that when God, glorified be He, described the state of the unbelievers when they are at a distance from Hell, He described their state when they are cast into it. We seek refuge in God from it with the most forceful of descriptions. Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: Regarding ﴿narrow﴾ (dayyiqan) there are two readings: with emphasis (tashdid) and without (takhfif), and the latter is the reading of Ibn Kathir.

The second issue: Several things have been related concerning the interpretation of narrowness. Qatadah said: Abdullah ibn Umar told us: "Jahannam will be so narrow for the disbeliever as the spike is narrow on the spear." The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about this and said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, they will be forced into the Fire as a peg is forced into a wall." Al-Kalbi said: The lower ones are lifted up by the flames, and the upper ones are pressed down by those who enter.

[Page 50]

فَيَزْدَحِمُونَ فِي تِلْكَ الأَبْوَابِ الضَّيِّقَةِ. قَالَ صَاحِبُ "al-Kashshaf" (الكَشّاف، تفسير الزمخشري): الكَرْبُ مَعَ الضِّيقِ، كَمَا أنَّ الرَّوْحَ مَعَ السَّعَةِ، وَلِذَلِكَ وَصَفَ اللَّهُ الجَنَّةَ بِأنَّ عَرْضَهَا السَّمَاوَاتُ وَالأَرْضُ، وَجَاءَ فِي الأَحَادِيثِ: "«إنَّ لِكُلِّ مُؤْمِنٍ مِنَ القُصُورِ وَالجِنَانِ كَذَا وَكَذَا»". وَلَقَدْ جَمَعَ اللَّهُ عَلَى أَهْلِ النَّارِ أَنْوَاعَ البَلَاءِ، حَيْثُ ضَمَّ إِلَى العَذَابِ الشَّدِيدِ الضِّيقَ.

المَسْأَلَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ: قَالُوا فِي تَفْسِيرِ قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿مُقَرَّنِينَ فِي الأَصْفَادِ﴾ [إبراهيم: ٤٩]: إنَّ أَهْلَ النَّارِ مَعَ مَا هُمْ فِيهِ مِنَ العَذَابِ الشَّدِيدِ وَالضِّيقِ الشَّدِيدِ يَكُونُونَ مُقَرَّنِينَ فِي السَّلَاسِلِ، قُرِنَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ إِلَى أَعْنَاقِهِمْ. وَقِيلَ: يُقْرَنُ مَعَ كُلِّ كَافِرٍ شَيْطَانُهُ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ، وَفِي أَرْجُلِهِمُ الأَصْفَادُ. ثُمَّ إنَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ حَكَى عَنْ أَهْلِ النَّارِ أَنَّهُمْ حِينَمَا يُشَاهِدُونَ هَذَا النَّوْعَ مِنَ العِقَابِ الشَّدِيدِ دَعَوْا ثُبُورًا، وَالثُّبُورُ: الهَلَاكُ، وَدُعَاؤُهُمْ أَنْ يَقُولُوا: وَاثُبُورَاهْ، أَيْ يَقُولُوا: يَا ثُبُورُ، هَذَا حِينُكَ وَزَمَانُكَ. وَرَوَى أَنَسٌ مَرْفُوعًا: "«أَوَّلُ مَنْ يُكْسَى حُلَّةً مِنَ النَّارِ إِبْلِيسُ، فَيَضَعُهَا عَلَى جَانِبَيْهِ وَيَسْحَبُهَا مِنْ خَلْفِهِ ذُرِّيَّتُهُ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ: يَا ثُبُورَاهْ، وَيُنَادَوْنَ: يَا ثُبُورَهُمْ حَتَّى يَرِدُوا النَّارَ»".

* * *

أَمَّا قَوْلُهُ: ﴿لَا تَدْعُوا الْيَوْمَ ثُبُورًا وَاحِدًا﴾ أَيْ: يُقَالُ لَهُمْ ذَلِكَ، وَهُمْ أَحِقَّاءُ بِأَنْ يُقَالَ لَهُمْ ذَلِكَ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ ثَمَّ قَوْلٌ. وَمَعْنَى ﴿وَادْعُوا ثُبُورًا كَثِيرًا﴾ أَنَّكُمْ وَقَعْتُمْ فِيمَا لَيْسَ ثُبُورُكُمْ مِنْهُ وَاحِدًا، إِنَّمَا هُوَ ثُبُورٌ كَثِيرٌ، إِمَّا لِأَنَّ العَذَابَ أَنْوَاعٌ وَأَلْوَانٌ، لِكُلِّ نَوْعٍ مِنْهَا ثُبُورٌ لِشِدَّتِهِ وَفَظَاعَتِهِ، أَوْ لِأَنَّهُمْ كُلَّمَا نَضِجَتْ جُلُودُهُمْ بُدِّلُوا غَيْرَهَا، أَوْ لِأَنَّ ذَلِكَ العَذَابَ دَائِمٌ خَالِصٌ عَنِ الشَّوْبِ، فَلَهُمْ فِي كُلِّ وَقْتٍ مِنَ الأَوْقَاتِ الَّتِي لَا نِهَايَةَ لَهَا ثُبُورٌ، أَوْ لِأَنَّهُمْ رُبَّمَا يَجِدُونَ بِسَبَبِ ذَلِكَ القَوْلِ نَوْعًا مِنَ الخِفَّةِ، فَإِنَّ المُعَذَّبَ إِذَا صَاحَ وَبَكَى وَجَدَ بِسَبَبِهِ نَوْعًا مِنَ الخِفَّةِ فَيُزْجَرُونَ عَنْ ذَلِكَ، وَيُخْبَرُونَ بِأَنَّ هَذَا الثُّبُورَ سَيَزْدَادُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ لِيَزْدَادَ حُزْنُهُمْ وَغَمُّهُمْ، نَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْهُ. قَالَ al-Kalbi (الكَلْبِيُّ): نَزَلَ هَذَا كُلُّهُ فِي حَقِّ أَبِي جَهْلٍ وَالكُفَّارِ الَّذِينَ ذَكَرُوا تِلْكَ الشُّبُهَاتِ.

[Page 47]

God Most High says: ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that: gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He will give you palaces.﴾ ﴿But they denied the Hour, and We have prepared a blazing Fire for those who deny the Hour.﴾ ﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they hear its raging and roaring.﴾ ﴿And when they are cast into a narrow place of it, bound together, they will cry out for destruction there.﴾ ﴿Do not cry out for one destruction today, but cry out for many destructions.﴾

Know that this is the second answer to that doubt. His words ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that﴾ mean: better than what they mentioned of worldly blessings, such as the treasure and the garden. He explained that "better" with His words ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He will give you palaces﴾. By this, He, glorified be He, draws attention to the fact that He is able to give the Messenger everything they mentioned. However, He Most High manages His servants according to what is beneficial, or according to the requirements of His will, and no one may object to Him regarding any of His actions. So He opens to one person the doors of knowledge and wisdom and closes to him the doors of worldly things, and it is the reverse for another. This is only because He does what He wills. Here there are several issues:

The first issue: Ibn Abbas said: "Better than that" means better than what they reproached you for lacking, which is the garden, because they reproached you for lacking a single garden, while He, glorified be He, is able to give you many gardens. In the narration of Ikrimah, He said: ﴿better than that﴾, meaning better than walking in the markets and seeking livelihood.

The second issue: His words ﴿if He wills﴾ mean that He, glorified be He, is able to do that, not that He Most High is in doubt, because doubt is not permissible concerning God Most High. Some people said: "If" here means "when," that is, We have already granted you gardens in the Hereafter and built palaces for you. He placed "if" only to alert the servants that one does not attain that except by His mercy, that it is contingent upon His pure will, and that no servant has any right over God, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter.

The third issue: "Qusur" is the plural of "qasr," which is an elevated dwelling. It is possible that each garden has a palace, so that it is both a dwelling and a place of recreation. It is also permissible that the palaces are plural and the gardens are plural. Mujahid said: "If He wills, He will give you gardens in the Hereafter and palaces in this world."

The fourth issue: Al-Farra' differed concerning His words ﴿and He will give﴾. Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim raised the lam (making it a nominative form, [wa-yaj'alu]), while others made it jussive. Whoever made it jussive means: if He wills, He will give you gardens and He will give you palaces. Whoever raised it means that it is a new sentence, and the meaning is: He will surely give you palaces. This is the view of al-Zajjaj. Al-Wahidi said: There is a difference in meaning between the two readings. According to the jussive reading, the meaning is: if He wills, He will give you palaces in this world, and it is not good to stop at "the rivers." According to the raised reading, it is good to stop at "the rivers" and begin anew, meaning: and He will give you palaces in the Hereafter. In the codex of Ubayy and Ibn Mas'ud it reads: "Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give."

The fifth issue: From Tawus, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "While the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was sitting, with Jibril (peace be upon him) beside him, Jibril (peace be upon him) said: This is an angel who has descended from the heavens, having asked his Lord for permission to visit you. He did not wait long before the angel came, greeted the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and said: 'God gives you the choice between being given the keys of everything that was not given to anyone before you and will not be given to anyone after you, without it diminishing for you anything of what He has stored up for you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Rather, let Him gather them all for me in the Hereafter.' Then the words ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills﴾ were revealed, to the end of the verse." And from Ibn Abbas, who said, peace be upon him: "Jibril offered me the gold of the valley of Mecca [Batha' Makkah], [page 48] and I said: 'Rather, a satisfied night and three hungry days,' and that is more for my remembrance and my request to my Lord." In the narration of Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Abd al-Wahhab, he (peace be upon him) said: "I eat my fill one day and go hungry three days; I praise You when I am satisfied, and I humble myself before You when I am hungry." And from al-Dahhak: "When the polytheists reproached the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for poverty, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) grieved over that. Then Jibril (peace be upon him) descended, consoling him, and said: 'God sends you His greetings and says: ﴿We did not send any messengers before you except that they ate food﴾ [al-Furqan: 20], to the end of the verse.'" He said: "While Jibril (peace be upon him) and the Prophet (ﷺ) were talking, a door of the gates of heaven opened that had not been opened before. Then he said: 'Rejoice, O Muhammad, this is Ridwan, keeper of the Garden. He has come to you with approval from your Lord.' So he greeted him and said: 'Your Lord gives you the choice between being a prophet-king and being a prophet-servant.' With him was a casket of light, shining. Then he said: 'These are the keys to the treasuries of this world; take them without God diminishing for you anything of what He has prepared for you in the Hereafter, not even the wing of a gnat.' The Prophet (ﷺ) looked at Jibril as one seeking counsel, and he gestured with his hand, meaning: humble yourself. So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'Rather, a prophet-servant.'" He said: After that, he (peace be upon him) never ate reclining until he departed this world.

* * *

As for God Most High's words ﴿But they denied the Hour, and We have prepared a blazing Fire for those who deny the Hour﴾, this is a third answer to that doubt. It is as if He, glorified be He, said: What they have clung to is not a doubt against you in itself; rather, what led them to deny you is their denial of the Hour, out of their reluctance to prepare for it. It is also possible that the meaning is that they deny the Hour, so they do not hope for reward or fear punishment, and they do not bear the burden of reflection and thought. Therefore they do not benefit from the proofs presented to them. Then He said: ﴿And We have prepared a blazing Fire for those who deny the Hour﴾. Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: Abu Muslim said: "And We have prepared" means: We made it ready and prepared for them. "Sa'ir" is a fierce fire of great blaze. From al-Hasan: it is one of the names of Jahannam (Hell).

The second issue: Our companions [the Ash'aris] argued that Paradise is created from His words ﴿It has been prepared for the God-fearing﴾ [Al 'Imran: 133], and that the Fire, which is the abode of punishment, is created from this verse, namely His words ﴿And We have prepared a blazing Fire for those who deny the Hour﴾. His words ﴿And We have prepared﴾ are a report of an act that occurred in the past, so the verse indicates that the abode of punishment is created. Al-Jubba'i said: "We have prepared" may mean the Fire in this world, with which God punishes the unbelievers and the wicked in their graves; and it may mean the Fire of the Hereafter, and the meaning of "We have prepared" would be: We will prepare it for them, as in His words: ﴿And the companions of the Garden will call out to the companions of the Fire﴾ [al-A'raf: 44]. Know that this objection is extremely weak, because what is meant by "sa'ir" is either the fire of this world or the fire of the Hereafter. If it is the first, then either the meaning is that He punishes them in this world with the fire of this world, or He punishes them in the Hereafter with the fire of this world. The first is false, because He did not punish them with fire in this world. The second is also false, because none of the community has said that God punishes the disbelievers in the Hereafter with the fires of this world. Therefore it is established that what is meant is the Fire of the Hereafter, and it is established that it is prepared. To interpret the verse as meaning that God will make it prepared is to abandon the apparent meaning without evidence. And since al-Hasan said that "sa'ir" is one of the names of Jahannam, His words ﴿And We have prepared a blazing Fire for those who deny the Hour﴾ are explicit that God has prepared Hell.

The third issue: Our companions argued by this verse that the one who is happy (sa'id) is the one who was made happy in his mother's womb. They said: Those for whom God has prepared the blazing Fire, and whom He reported and decreed for that, if they became believers among the people of reward, then God's judgment that they are among the people of the Fire would have become false, and His knowledge would have become ignorance. This reversal is impossible, and whatever leads to the impossible is impossible. Therefore, the transformation of those people into believers among the people of reward is impossible. It is thus established that the happy one does not become wretched, and the wretched one does not become happy.

Girding a sword and a spear.

The fourth issue: Ubayd ibn Umayr said: Jahannam emits a roar such that no one remains without his limbs trembling, until Ibrahim (peace be upon him) falls on his knees saying: "Myself, myself!"

The second attribute of the Fire: God Most High's words ﴿And when they are cast into a narrow place of it, bound together, they will cry out for destruction there.﴾ Know that when God, glorified be He, described the state of the unbelievers when they are at a distance from Hell, He described their state when they are cast into it. The first issue: Regarding ﴿narrow﴾ (dayyiqan) there are two readings: with emphasis (tashdid) and without (takhfif), and the latter is the reading of Ibn Kathir.

The second issue: Several things have been related concerning the interpretation of narrowness. Qatadah said: Abdullah ibn Umar told us: "Jahannam will be so narrow for the disbeliever as the spike is narrow on the spear." The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about this and said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, they will be forced into the Fire as a peg is forced into a wall." Al-Kalbi said: The lower ones are lifted up by the flames, and the upper ones are pressed down by those who enter.

[Page 50]

فَيَزْدَحِمُونَ فِي تِلْكَ الأَبْوَابِ الضَّيِّقَةِ. قَالَ صَاحِبُ "al-Kashshaf" (الكَشّاف، تفسير الزمخشري): الكَرْبُ مَعَ الضِّيقِ، كَمَا أنَّ الرَّوْحَ مَعَ السَّعَةِ، وَلِذَلِكَ وَصَفَ اللَّهُ الجَنَّةَ بِأنَّ عَرْضَهَا السَّمَاوَاتُ وَالأَرْضُ، وَجَاءَ فِي الأَحَادِيثِ: "«إنَّ لِكُلِّ مُؤْمِنٍ مِنَ القُصُورِ وَالجِنَانِ كَذَا وَكَذَا»". وَلَقَدْ جَمَعَ اللَّهُ عَلَى أَهْلِ النَّارِ أَنْوَاعَ البَلَاءِ، حَيْثُ ضَمَّ إِلَى العَذَابِ الشَّدِيدِ الضِّيقَ.

المَسْأَلَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ: قَالُوا فِي تَفْسِيرِ قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿مُقَرَّنِينَ فِي الأَصْفَادِ﴾ [إبراهيم: ٤٩]: إنَّ أَهْلَ النَّارِ مَعَ مَا هُمْ فِيهِ مِنَ العَذَابِ الشَّدِيدِ وَالضِّيقِ الشَّدِيدِ يَكُونُونَ مُقَرَّنِينَ فِي السَّلَاسِلِ، قُرِنَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ إِلَى أَعْنَاقِهِمْ. وَقِيلَ: يُقْرَنُ مَعَ كُلِّ كَافِرٍ شَيْطَانُهُ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ، وَفِي أَرْجُلِهِمُ الأَصْفَادُ. ثُمَّ إنَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ حَكَى عَنْ أَهْلِ النَّارِ أَنَّهُمْ حِينَمَا يُشَاهِدُونَ هَذَا النَّوْعَ مِنَ العِقَابِ الشَّدِيدِ دَعَوْا ثُبُورًا، وَالثُّبُورُ: الهَلَاكُ، وَدُعَاؤُهُمْ أَنْ يَقُولُوا: وَاثُبُورَاهْ، أَيْ يَقُولُوا: يَا ثُبُورُ، هَذَا حِينُكَ وَزَمَانُكَ. وَرَوَى أَنَسٌ مَرْفُوعًا: "«أَوَّلُ مَنْ يُكْسَى حُلَّةً مِنَ النَّارِ إِبْلِيسُ، فَيَضَعُهَا عَلَى جَانِبَيْهِ وَيَسْحَبُهَا مِنْ خَلْفِهِ ذُرِّيَّتُهُ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ: يَا ثُبُورَاهْ، وَيُنَادَوْنَ: يَا ثُبُورَهُمْ حَتَّى يَرِدُوا النَّارَ»".

* * *

أَمَّا قَوْلُهُ: ﴿لَا تَدْعُوا الْيَوْمَ ثُبُورًا وَاحِدًا﴾ أَيْ: يُقَالُ لَهُمْ ذَلِكَ، وَهُمْ أَحِقَّاءُ بِأَنْ يُقَالَ لَهُمْ ذَلِكَ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ ثَمَّ قَوْلٌ. وَمَعْنَى ﴿وَادْعُوا ثُبُورًا كَثِيرًا﴾ أَنَّكُمْ وَقَعْتُمْ فِيمَا لَيْسَ ثُبُورُكُمْ مِنْهُ وَاحِدًا، إِنَّمَا هُوَ ثُبُورٌ كَثِيرٌ، إِمَّا لِأَنَّ العَذَابَ أَنْوَاعٌ وَأَلْوَانٌ، لِكُلِّ نَوْعٍ مِنْهَا ثُبُورٌ لِشِدَّتِهِ وَفَظَاعَتِهِ، أَوْ لِأَنَّهُمْ كُلَّمَا نَضِجَتْ جُلُودُهُمْ بُدِّلُوا غَيْرَهَا، أَوْ لِأَنَّ ذَلِكَ العَذَابَ دَائِمٌ خَالِصٌ عَنِ الشَّوْبِ، فَلَهُمْ فِي كُلِّ وَقْتٍ مِنَ الأَوْقَاتِ الَّتِي لَا نِهَايَةَ لَهَا ثُبُورٌ، أَوْ لِأَنَّهُمْ رُبَّمَا يَجِدُونَ بِسَبَبِ ذَلِكَ القَوْلِ نَوْعًا مِنَ الخِفَّةِ، فَإِنَّ المُعَذَّبَ إِذَا صَاحَ وَبَكَى وَجَدَ بِسَبَبِهِ نَوْعًا مِنَ الخِفَّةِ فَيُزْجَرُونَ عَنْ ذَلِكَ، وَيُخْبَرُونَ بِأَنَّ هَذَا الثُّبُورَ سَيَزْدَادُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ لِيَزْدَادَ حُزْنُهُمْ وَغَمُّهُمْ، نَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْهُ. قَالَ al-Kalbi (الكَلْبِيُّ): نَزَلَ هَذَا كُلُّهُ فِي حَقِّ أَبِي جَهْلٍ وَالكُفَّارِ الَّذِينَ ذَكَرُوا تِلْكَ الشُّبُهَاتِ.

[Page 47]

God Most High says: ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that: gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He will give you palaces.﴾ ﴿But they denied the Hour, and We have prepared a blazing Fire for those who deny the Hour.﴾ ﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they hear its raging and roaring.﴾ ﴿And when they are cast into a narrow place of it, bound together, they will cry out for destruction there.﴾ ﴿Do not cry out for one destruction today, but cry out for many destructions.﴾

Know that this is the second answer to that doubt. His words ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that﴾ mean: better than what they mentioned of worldly blessings, such as the treasure and the garden. He explained that "better" with His words ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He will give you palaces﴾. By this, He, glorified be He, draws attention to the fact that He is able to give the Messenger everything they mentioned. However, He Most High manages His servants according to what is beneficial, or according to the requirements of His will, and no one may object to Him regarding any of His actions. So He opens to one person the doors of knowledge and wisdom and closes to him the doors of worldly things, and it is the reverse for another. This is only because He does what He wills. Here there are several issues:

The first issue: Ibn Abbas said: "Better than that" means better than what they reproached you for lacking, which is the garden, because they reproached you for lacking a single garden, while He, glorified be He, is able to give you many gardens. In the narration of Ikrimah, He said: ﴿better than that﴾, meaning better than walking in the markets and seeking livelihood.

The second issue: His words ﴿if He wills﴾ mean that He, glorified be He, is able to do that, not that He Most High is in doubt, because doubt is not permissible concerning God Most High. Some people said: "If" here means "when," that is, We have already granted you gardens in the Hereafter and built palaces for you. He placed "if" only to alert the servants that one does not attain that except by His mercy, that it is contingent upon His pure will, and that no servant has any right over God, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter.

The third issue: "Qusur" is the plural of "qasr," which is an elevated dwelling. It is possible that each garden has a palace, so that it is both a dwelling and a place of recreation. It is also permissible that the palaces are plural and the gardens are plural. Mujahid said: "If He wills, He will give you gardens in the Hereafter and palaces in this world."

The fourth issue: Al-Farra' differed concerning His words ﴿and He will give﴾. Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim raised the lam (making it a nominative form, [wa-yaj'alu]), while others made it jussive. Whoever made it jussive means: if He wills, He will give you gardens and He will give you palaces. Whoever raised it means that it is a new sentence, and the meaning is: He will surely give you palaces. This is the view of al-Zajjaj. Al-Wahidi said: There is a difference in meaning between the two readings. According to the jussive reading, the meaning is: if He wills, He will give you palaces in this world, and it is not good to stop at "the rivers." According to the raised reading, it is good to stop at "the rivers" and begin anew, meaning: and He will give you palaces in the Hereafter. In the codex of Ubayy and Ibn Mas'ud it reads: "Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give."

The fifth issue: From Tawus, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "While the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was sitting, with Jibril (peace be upon him) beside him, Jibril (peace be upon him) said: This is an angel who has descended from the heavens, having asked his Lord for permission to visit you. He did not wait long before the angel came, greeted the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and said: 'God gives you the choice between being given the keys of everything that was not given to anyone before you and will not be given to anyone after you, without it diminishing for you anything of what He has stored up for you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Rather, let Him gather them all for me in the Hereafter.' Then the words ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills﴾ were revealed, to the end of the verse." And from Ibn Abbas, who said, peace be upon him: "Jibril offered me the gold of the valley of Mecca [Batha' Makkah], [page 48] and I said: 'Rather, a satisfied night and three hungry days,' and that is more for my remembrance and my request to my Lord." In the narration of Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Abd al-Wahhab, he (peace be upon him) said: "I eat my fill one day and go hungry three days; I praise You when I am satisfied, and I humble myself before You when I am hungry." And from al-Dahhak: "When the polytheists reproached the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for poverty, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) grieved over that. Then Jibril (peace be upon him) descended, consoling him, and said: 'God sends you His greetings and says: ﴿We did not send any messengers before you except that they ate food﴾ [al-Furqan: 20], to the end of the verse.'" He said: "While Jibril (peace be upon him) and the Prophet (ﷺ) were talking, a door of the gates of heaven opened that had not been opened before. Then he said: 'Rejoice, O Muhammad, this is Ridwan, keeper of the Garden. He has come to you with approval from your Lord.' So he greeted him and said: 'Your Lord gives you the choice between being a prophet-king and being a prophet-servant.' With him was a casket of light, shining. Then he said: 'These are the keys to the treasuries of this world; take them without God diminishing for you anything of what He has prepared for you in the Hereafter, not even the wing of a gnat.' The Prophet (ﷺ) looked at Jibril as one seeking counsel, and he gestured with his hand, meaning: humble yourself. So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'Rather, a prophet-servant.'" He said: After that, he (peace be upon him) never ate reclining until he departed this world.

* * *

As for God Most High's words ﴿But they denied the Hour, and We have prepared a blazing Fire for those who deny the Hour﴾, this is a third answer to that doubt. It is as if He, glorified be He, said: What they have clung to is not a doubt against you in itself; rather, what led them to deny you is their denial of the Hour, out of their reluctance to prepare for it. It is also possible that the meaning is that they deny the Hour, so they do not hope for reward or fear punishment, and they do not bear the burden of reflection and thought. Therefore they do not benefit from the proofs presented to them. Then He said: ﴿And We have prepared a blazing Fire for those who deny the Hour﴾. Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: Abu Muslim said: "And We have prepared" means: We made it ready and prepared for them. "Sa'ir" is a fierce fire of great blaze. From al-Hasan: it is one of the names of Jahannam (Hell).

The second issue: Our companions [the Ash'aris] argued that Paradise is created from His words ﴿It has been prepared for the God-fearing﴾ [Al 'Imran: 133], and that the Fire, which is the abode of punishment, is created from this verse, namely His words ﴿And We have prepared a blazing Fire for those who deny the Hour﴾. His words ﴿And We have prepared﴾ are a report of an act that occurred in the past, so the verse indicates that the abode of punishment is created. Al-Jubba'i said: "We have prepared" may mean the Fire in this world, with which God punishes the unbelievers and the wicked in their graves; and it may mean the Fire of the Hereafter, and the meaning of "We have prepared" would be: We will prepare it for them, as in His words: ﴿And the companions of the Garden will call out to the companions of the Fire﴾ [al-A'raf: 44]. Know that this objection is extremely weak, because what is meant by "sa'ir" is either the fire of this world or the fire of the Hereafter. If it is the first, then either the meaning is that He punishes them in this world with the fire of this world, or He punishes them in the Hereafter with the fire of this world. The first is false, because He did not punish them with fire in this world. The second is also false, because none of the community has said that God punishes the disbelievers in the Hereafter with the fires of this world. Therefore it is established that what is meant is the Fire of the Hereafter, and it is established that it is prepared. To interpret the verse as meaning that God will make it prepared is to abandon the apparent meaning without evidence. And since al-Hasan said that "sa'ir" is one of the names of Jahannam, His words ﴿And We have prepared a blazing Fire for those who deny the Hour﴾ are explicit that God has prepared Hell.

The third issue: Our companions argued by this verse that the one who is happy (sa'id) is the one who was made happy in his mother's womb. They said: Those for whom God has prepared the blazing Fire, and whom He reported and decreed for that, if they became believers among the people of reward, then God's judgment that they are among the people of the Fire would have become false, and His knowledge would have become ignorance. This reversal is impossible, and whatever leads to the impossible is impossible. Therefore, the transformation of those people into believers among the people of reward is impossible. It is thus established that the happy one does not become wretched, and the wretched one does not become happy.

* * *

Then, glorified and exalted be He, described the blazing Fire with attributes:

[Page 49] The first of them is His words: ﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they hear its raging and roaring.﴾ Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: "Sa'ir" is masculine, but here it appears feminine, because He said ﴿saw them﴾ and ﴿they heard for it﴾. It came feminine according to the meaning of "fire" (nar).

The second issue: The doctrine of our companions is that life is not conditional upon bodily structure. Thus the fire, in its present state, may have life, reason and speech created in it by God. For the Mu'tazilah (the rationalist school), this is not permissible. These Mu'tazilah have no proof in this matter except the extrapolation from habitual experience. Even if that were true, it would necessitate denying the breaking of habits in the case of the messengers. So their position is self-contradictory. Rather, rejecting habits befits only the principles of the philosophers. Accordingly, our companions said: God's words describing the Fire, ﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they hear its raging and roaring﴾, must be taken in their apparent sense, because there is no impossibility in the Fire being living, seeing, and enraged against the disbelievers. As for the Mu'tazilah, they had to resort to interpretation, and they mentioned several ways of doing so:

One of them: They said: "It sees them" means "it appears to them," from the expression "their houses are in view of each other" (tatarra'a), meaning they face each other. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "The fires of a believer and an unbeliever do not see each other," meaning they do not face each other, because the believer is obliged to keep away from the unbeliever and the polytheist. It is said: "The houses of so-and-so are facing," meaning they are opposite each other.

The second: The Fire, because of the intensity of its blazing and boiling, becomes as if it sees the unbelievers, seeks them out, and rages against them.

The third: Al-Jubba'i said: God mentioned the Fire but meant the guardians entrusted with punishing the people of the Fire, because seeing is possible for them but not for the Fire. It is like His words ﴿and ask the town﴾ [Yusuf: 82], meaning its people.

The third issue: One may say: Raging is an expression for intense anger, and that cannot be heard. How then did God say ﴿they heard for it raging and roaring﴾? The answer to this has several aspects:

The first: Although raging cannot be heard, what indicates it may be heard, namely a sound. It is like saying: "I saw the anger of the commander against so-and-so," when one sees what indicates it. The same is said about love. So here too: they heard for it a sound resembling the sound of one who rages. This is the view of al-Zajjaj.

The second: The meaning is: they knew of its raging and heard its roaring. This is the view of Qutrub, and it is like the words of the poet:

Girding a sword and a spear.

The third: What is meant is the raging of the guardians.

The fourth issue: Ubayd ibn Umayr said: Jahannam emits a roar such that no one remains without his limbs trembling, until Ibrahim (peace be upon him) falls on his knees saying: "Myself, myself!"

* * *

The second attribute of the Fire: God Most High's words ﴿And when they are cast into a narrow place of it, bound together, they will cry out for destruction there.﴾ Know that when God, glorified be He, described the state of the unbelievers when they are at a distance from Hell, He described their state when they are cast into it. We seek refuge in God from it with the most forceful of descriptions. Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: Regarding ﴿narrow﴾ (dayyiqan) there are two readings: with emphasis (tashdid) and without (takhfif), and the latter is the reading of Ibn Kathir.

The second issue: Several things have been related concerning the interpretation of narrowness. Qatadah said: Abdullah ibn Umar told us: "Jahannam will be so narrow for the disbeliever as the spike is narrow on the spear." The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about this and said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, they will be forced into the Fire as a peg is forced into a wall." Al-Kalbi said: The lower ones are lifted up by the flames, and the upper ones are pressed down by those who enter.

المَسْأَلَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ: قَالُوا فِي تَفْسِيرِ قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿مُقَرَّنِينَ فِي الأَصْفَادِ﴾ [إبراهيم: ٤٩]: إنَّ أَهْلَ النَّارِ مَعَ مَا هُمْ فِيهِ مِنَ العَذَابِ الشَّدِيدِ وَالضِّيقِ الشَّدِيدِ يَكُونُونَ مُقَرَّنِينَ فِي السَّلَاسِلِ، قُرِنَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ إِلَى أَعْنَاقِهِمْ. وَقِيلَ: يُقْرَنُ مَعَ كُلِّ كَافِرٍ شَيْطَانُهُ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ، وَفِي أَرْجُلِهِمُ الأَصْفَادُ. ثُمَّ إنَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ حَكَى عَنْ أَهْلِ النَّارِ أَنَّهُمْ حِينَمَا يُشَاهِدُونَ هَذَا النَّوْعَ مِنَ العِقَابِ الشَّدِيدِ دَعَوْا ثُبُورًا، وَالثُّبُورُ: الهَلَاكُ، وَدُعَاؤُهُمْ أَنْ يَقُولُوا: وَاثُبُورَاهْ، أَيْ يَقُولُوا: يَا ثُبُورُ، هَذَا حِينُكَ وَزَمَانُكَ. وَرَوَى أَنَسٌ مَرْفُوعًا: "«أَوَّلُ مَنْ يُكْسَى حُلَّةً مِنَ النَّارِ إِبْلِيسُ، فَيَضَعُهَا عَلَى جَانِبَيْهِ وَيَسْحَبُهَا مِنْ خَلْفِهِ ذُرِّيَّتُهُ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ: يَا ثُبُورَاهْ، وَيُنَادَوْنَ: يَا ثُبُورَهُمْ حَتَّى يَرِدُوا النَّارَ»".

* * *

أَمَّا قَوْلُهُ: ﴿لَا تَدْعُوا الْيَوْمَ ثُبُورًا وَاحِدًا﴾ أَيْ: يُقَالُ لَهُمْ ذَلِكَ، وَهُمْ أَحِقَّاءُ بِأَنْ يُقَالَ لَهُمْ ذَلِكَ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ ثَمَّ قَوْلٌ. وَمَعْنَى ﴿وَادْعُوا ثُبُورًا كَثِيرًا﴾ أَنَّكُمْ وَقَعْتُمْ فِيمَا لَيْسَ ثُبُورُكُمْ مِنْهُ وَاحِدًا، إِنَّمَا هُوَ ثُبُورٌ كَثِيرٌ، إِمَّا لِأَنَّ العَذَابَ أَنْوَاعٌ وَأَلْوَانٌ، لِكُلِّ نَوْعٍ مِنْهَا ثُبُورٌ لِشِدَّتِهِ وَفَظَاعَتِهِ، أَوْ لِأَنَّهُمْ كُلَّمَا نَضِجَتْ جُلُودُهُمْ بُدِّلُوا غَيْرَهَا، أَوْ لِأَنَّ ذَلِكَ العَذَابَ دَائِمٌ خَالِصٌ عَنِ الشَّوْبِ، فَلَهُمْ فِي كُلِّ وَقْتٍ مِنَ الأَوْقَاتِ الَّتِي لَا نِهَايَةَ لَهَا ثُبُورٌ، أَوْ لِأَنَّهُمْ رُبَّمَا يَجِدُونَ بِسَبَبِ ذَلِكَ القَوْلِ نَوْعًا مِنَ الخِفَّةِ، فَإِنَّ المُعَذَّبَ إِذَا صَاحَ وَبَكَى وَجَدَ بِسَبَبِهِ نَوْعًا مِنَ الخِفَّةِ فَيُزْجَرُونَ عَنْ ذَلِكَ، وَيُخْبَرُونَ بِأَنَّ هَذَا الثُّبُورَ سَيَزْدَادُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ لِيَزْدَادَ حُزْنُهُمْ وَغَمُّهُمْ، نَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْهُ. قَالَ al-Kalbi (الكَلْبِيُّ): نَزَلَ هَذَا كُلُّهُ فِي حَقِّ أَبِي جَهْلٍ وَالكُفَّارِ الَّذِينَ ذَكَرُوا تِلْكَ الشُّبُهَاتِ.

[Page 47]

God Most High says: ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that: gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He will give you palaces.﴾ ﴿But they denied the Hour, and We have prepared a blazing Fire for those who deny the Hour.﴾ ﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they hear its raging and roaring.﴾ ﴿And when they are cast into a narrow place of it, bound together, they will cry out for destruction there.﴾ ﴿Do not cry out for one destruction today, but cry out for many destructions.﴾

Know that this is the second answer to that doubt. His words ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that﴾ mean: better than what they mentioned of worldly blessings, such as the treasure and the garden. He explained that "better" with His words ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He will give you palaces﴾. By this, He, glorified be He, draws attention to the fact that He is able to give the Messenger everything they mentioned. However, He Most High manages His servants according to what is beneficial, or according to the requirements of His will, and no one may object to Him regarding any of His actions. So He opens to one person the doors of knowledge and wisdom and closes to him the doors of worldly things, and it is the reverse for another. This is only because He does what He wills. Here there are several issues:

The first issue: Ibn Abbas said: "Better than that" means better than what they reproached you for lacking, which is the garden, because they reproached you for lacking a single garden, while He, glorified be He, is able to give you many gardens. In the narration of Ikrimah, He said: ﴿better than that﴾, meaning better than walking in the markets and seeking livelihood.

The second issue: His words ﴿if He wills﴾ mean that He, glorified be He, is able to do that, not that He Most High is in doubt, because doubt is not permissible concerning God Most High. Some people said: "If" here means "when," that is, We have already granted you gardens in the Hereafter and built palaces for you. He placed "if" only to alert the servants that one does not attain that except by His mercy, that it is contingent upon His pure will, and that no servant has any right over God, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter.

The third issue: "Qusur" is the plural of "qasr," which is an elevated dwelling. It is possible that each garden has a palace, so that it is both a dwelling and a place of recreation. It is also permissible that the palaces are plural and the gardens are plural. Mujahid said: "If He wills, He will give you gardens in the Hereafter and palaces in this world."

The fourth issue: Al-Farra' differed concerning His words ﴿and He will give﴾. Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim raised the lam (making it a nominative form, [wa-yaj'alu]), while others made it jussive. Whoever made it jussive means: if He wills, He will give you gardens and He will give you palaces. Whoever raised it means that it is a new sentence, and the meaning is: He will surely give you palaces. This is the view of al-Zajjaj. Al-Wahidi said: There is a difference in meaning between the two readings. According to the jussive reading, the meaning is: if He wills, He will give you palaces in this world, and it is not good to stop at "the rivers." According to the raised reading, it is good to stop at "the rivers" and begin anew, meaning: and He will give you palaces in the Hereafter. In the codex of Ubayy and Ibn Mas'ud it reads: "Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give."

The fifth issue: From Tawus, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "While the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was sitting, with Jibril (peace be upon him) beside him, Jibril (peace be upon him) said: This is an angel who has descended from the heavens, having asked his Lord for permission to visit you. He did not wait long before the angel came, greeted the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and said: 'God gives you the choice between being given the keys of everything that was not given to anyone before you and will not be given to anyone after you, without it diminishing for you anything of what He has stored up for you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Rather, let Him gather them all for me in the Hereafter.' Then the words ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills﴾ were revealed, to the end of the verse." And from Ibn Abbas, who said, peace be upon him: "Jibril offered me the gold of the valley of Mecca [Batha' Makkah], [page 48] and I said: 'Rather, a satisfied night and three hungry days,' and that is more for my remembrance and my request to my Lord." In the narration of Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Abd al-Wahhab, he (peace be upon him) said: "I eat my fill one day and go hungry three days; I praise You when I am satisfied, and I humble myself before You when I am hungry." And from al-Dahhak: "When the polytheists reproached the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for poverty, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) grieved over that. Then Jibril (peace be upon him) descended, consoling him, and said: 'God sends you His greetings and says: ﴿We did not send any messengers before you except that they ate food﴾ [al-Furqan: 20], to the end of the verse.'" He said: "While Jibril (peace be upon him) and the Prophet (ﷺ) were talking, a door of the gates of heaven opened that had not been opened before. Then he said: 'Rejoice, O Muhammad, this is Ridwan, keeper of the Garden. He has come to you with approval from your Lord.' So he greeted him and said: 'Your Lord gives you the choice between being a prophet-king and being a prophet-servant.' With him was a casket of light, shining. Then he said: 'These are the keys to the treasuries of this world; take them without God diminishing for you anything of what He has prepared for you in the Hereafter, not even the wing of a gnat.' The Prophet (ﷺ) looked at Jibril as one seeking counsel, and he gestured with his hand, meaning: humble yourself. So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'Rather, a prophet-servant.'" He said: After that, he (peace be upon him) never ate reclining until he departed this world.

* * *

As for God Most High's words ﴿But they denied the Hour, and We have prepared a blazing Fire for those who deny the Hour﴾, this is a third answer to that doubt. It is as if He, glorified be He, said: What they have clung to is not a doubt against you in itself; rather, what led them to deny you is their denial of the Hour, out of their reluctance to prepare for it. It is also possible that the meaning is that they deny the Hour, so they do not hope for reward or fear punishment, and they do not bear the burden of reflection and thought. Therefore they do not benefit from the proofs presented to them. Then He said: ﴿And We have prepared a blazing Fire for those who deny the Hour﴾. Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: Abu Muslim said: "And We have prepared" means: We made it ready and prepared for them. "Sa'ir" is a fierce fire of great blaze. From al-Hasan: it is one of the names of Jahannam (Hell).

The second issue: Our companions [the Ash'aris] argued that Paradise is created from His words ﴿It has been prepared for the God-fearing﴾ [Al 'Imran: 133], and that the Fire, which is the abode of punishment, is created from this verse, namely His words ﴿And We have prepared a blazing Fire for those who deny the Hour﴾. His words ﴿And We have prepared﴾ are a report of an act that occurred in the past, so the verse indicates that the abode of punishment is created. Al-Jubba'i said: "We have prepared" may mean the Fire in this world, with which God punishes the unbelievers and the wicked in their graves; and it may mean the Fire of the Hereafter, and the meaning of "We have prepared" would be: We will prepare it for them, as in His words: ﴿And the companions of the Garden will call out to the companions of the Fire﴾ [al-A'raf: 44]. Know that this objection is extremely weak, because what is meant by "sa'ir" is either the fire of this world or the fire of the Hereafter. If it is the first, then either the meaning is that He punishes them in this world with the fire of this world, or He punishes them in the Hereafter with the fire of this world. The first is false, because He did not punish them with fire in this world. The second is also false, because none of the community has said that God punishes the disbelievers in the Hereafter with the fires of this world. Therefore it is established that what is meant is the Fire of the Hereafter, and it is established that it is prepared. To interpret the verse as meaning that God will make it prepared is to abandon the apparent meaning without evidence. And since al-Hasan said that "sa'ir" is one of the names of Jahannam, His words ﴿And We have prepared a blazing Fire for those who deny the Hour﴾ are explicit that God has prepared Hell.

The third issue: Our companions argued by this verse that the one who is happy (sa'id) is the one who was made happy in his mother's womb. They said: Those for whom God has prepared the blazing Fire, and whom He reported and decreed for that, if they became believers among the people of reward, then God's judgment that they are among the people of the Fire would have become false, and His knowledge would have become ignorance. This reversal is impossible, and whatever leads to the impossible is impossible. Therefore, the transformation of those people into believers among the people of reward is impossible. It is thus established that the happy one does not become wretched, and the wretched one does not become happy.

* * *

Then, glorified and exalted be He, described the blazing Fire with attributes:

[Page 49] The first of them is His words: ﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they hear its raging and roaring.﴾ Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: "Sa'ir" is masculine, but here it appears feminine, because He said ﴿saw them﴾ and ﴿they heard for it﴾. It came feminine according to the meaning of "fire" (nar).

The second issue: The doctrine of our companions is that life is not conditional upon bodily structure. Thus the fire, in its present state, may have life, reason and speech created in it by God. For the Mu'tazilah (the rationalist school), this is not permissible. These Mu'tazilah have no proof in this matter except the extrapolation from habitual experience. Even if that were true, it would necessitate denying the breaking of habits in the case of the messengers. So their position is self-contradictory. Rather, rejecting habits befits only the principles of the philosophers. Accordingly, our companions said: God's words describing the Fire, ﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they hear its raging and roaring﴾, must be taken in their apparent sense, because there is no impossibility in the Fire being living, seeing, and enraged against the disbelievers. As for the Mu'tazilah, they had to resort to interpretation, and they mentioned several ways of doing so:

One of them: They said: "It sees them" means "it appears to them," from the expression "their houses are in view of each other" (tatarra'a), meaning they face each other. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "The fires of a believer and an unbeliever do not see each other," meaning they do not face each other, because the believer is obliged to keep away from the unbeliever and the polytheist. It is said: "The houses of so-and-so are facing," meaning they are opposite each other.

The second: The Fire, because of the intensity of its blazing and boiling, becomes as if it sees the unbelievers, seeks them out, and rages against them.

The third: Al-Jubba'i said: God mentioned the Fire but meant the guardians entrusted with punishing the people of the Fire, because seeing is possible for them but not for the Fire. It is like His words ﴿and ask the town﴾ [Yusuf: 82], meaning its people.

The third issue: One may say: Raging is an expression for intense anger, and that cannot be heard. How then did God say ﴿they heard for it raging and roaring﴾? The answer to this has several aspects:

The first: Although raging cannot be heard, what indicates it may be heard, namely a sound. It is like saying: "I saw the anger of the commander against so-and-so," when one sees what indicates it. The same is said about love. So here too: they heard for it a sound resembling the sound of one who rages. This is the view of al-Zajjaj.

The second: The meaning is: they knew of its raging and heard its roaring. This is the view of Qutrub, and it is like the words of the poet:

Girding a sword and a spear.

The third: What is meant is the raging of the guardians.

The fourth issue: Ubayd ibn Umayr said: Jahannam emits a roar such that no one remains without his limbs trembling, until Ibrahim (peace be upon him) falls on his knees saying: "Myself, myself!"

* * *

The second attribute of the Fire: God Most High's words ﴿And when they are cast into a narrow place of it, bound together, they will cry out for destruction there.﴾ Know that when God, glorified be He, described the state of the unbelievers when they are at a distance from Hell, He described their state when they are cast into it. We seek refuge in God from it with the most forceful of descriptions. Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: Regarding ﴿narrow﴾ (dayyiqan) there are two readings: with emphasis (tashdid) and without (takhfif), and the latter is the reading of Ibn Kathir.

The second issue: Several things have been related concerning the interpretation of narrowness. Qatadah said: Abdullah ibn Umar told us: "Jahannam will be so narrow for the disbeliever as the spike is narrow on the spear." The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about this and said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, they will be forced into the Fire as a peg is forced into a wall." Al-Kalbi said: The lower ones are lifted up by the flames, and the upper ones are pressed down by those who enter.

[Page 50]

فَيَزْدَحِمُونَ فِي تِلْكَ الأَبْوَابِ الضَّيِّقَةِ. قَالَ صَاحِبُ "al-Kashshaf" (الكَشّاف، تفسير الزمخشري): الكَرْبُ مَعَ الضِّيقِ، كَمَا أنَّ الرَّوْحَ مَعَ السَّعَةِ، وَلِذَلِكَ وَصَفَ اللَّهُ الجَنَّةَ بِأنَّ عَرْضَهَا السَّمَاوَاتُ وَالأَرْضُ، وَجَاءَ فِي الأَحَادِيثِ: "«إنَّ لِكُلِّ مُؤْمِنٍ مِنَ القُصُورِ وَالجِنَانِ كَذَا وَكَذَا»". وَلَقَدْ جَمَعَ اللَّهُ عَلَى أَهْلِ النَّارِ أَنْوَاعَ البَلَاءِ، حَيْثُ ضَمَّ إِلَى العَذَابِ الشَّدِيدِ الضِّيقَ.

المَسْأَلَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ: قَالُوا فِي تَفْسِيرِ قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿مُقَرَّنِينَ فِي الأَصْفَادِ﴾ [إبراهيم: ٤٩]: إنَّ أَهْلَ النَّارِ مَعَ مَا هُمْ فِيهِ مِنَ العَذَابِ الشَّدِيدِ وَالضِّيقِ الشَّدِيدِ يَكُونُونَ مُقَرَّنِينَ فِي السَّلَاسِلِ، قُرِنَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ إِلَى أَعْنَاقِهِمْ. وَقِيلَ: يُقْرَنُ مَعَ كُلِّ كَافِرٍ شَيْطَانُهُ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ، وَفِي أَرْجُلِهِمُ الأَصْفَادُ. ثُمَّ إنَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ حَكَى عَنْ أَهْلِ النَّارِ أَنَّهُمْ حِينَمَا يُشَاهِدُونَ هَذَا النَّوْعَ مِنَ العِقَابِ الشَّدِيدِ دَعَوْا ثُبُورًا، وَالثُّبُورُ: الهَلَاكُ، وَدُعَاؤُهُمْ أَنْ يَقُولُوا: وَاثُبُورَاهْ، أَيْ يَقُولُوا: يَا ثُبُورُ، هَذَا حِينُكَ وَزَمَانُكَ. وَرَوَى أَنَسٌ مَرْفُوعًا: "«أَوَّلُ مَنْ يُكْسَى حُلَّةً مِنَ النَّارِ إِبْلِيسُ، فَيَضَعُهَا عَلَى جَانِبَيْهِ وَيَسْحَبُهَا مِنْ خَلْفِهِ ذُرِّيَّتُهُ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ: يَا ثُبُورَاهْ، وَيُنَادَوْنَ: يَا ثُبُورَهُمْ حَتَّى يَرِدُوا النَّارَ»".

أَمَّا قَوْلُهُ: ﴿لَا تَدْعُوا الْيَوْمَ ثُبُورًا وَاحِدًا﴾ أَيْ: يُقَالُ لَهُمْ ذَلِكَ، وَهُمْ أَحِقَّاءُ بِأَنْ يُقَالَ لَهُمْ ذَلِكَ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ ثَمَّ قَوْلٌ. وَمَعْنَى ﴿وَادْعُوا ثُبُورًا كَثِيرًا﴾ أَنَّكُمْ وَقَعْتُمْ فِيمَا لَيْسَ ثُبُورُكُمْ مِنْهُ وَاحِدًا، إِنَّمَا هُوَ ثُبُورٌ كَثِيرٌ، إِمَّا لِأَنَّ العَذَابَ أَنْوَاعٌ وَأَلْوَانٌ، لِكُلِّ نَوْعٍ مِنْهَا ثُبُورٌ لِشِدَّتِهِ وَفَظَاعَتِهِ، أَوْ لِأَنَّهُمْ كُلَّمَا نَضِجَتْ جُلُودُهُمْ بُدِّلُوا غَيْرَهَا، أَوْ لِأَنَّ ذَلِكَ العَذَابَ دَائِمٌ خَالِصٌ عَنِ الشَّوْبِ، فَلَهُمْ فِي كُلِّ وَقْتٍ مِنَ الأَوْقَاتِ الَّتِي لَا نِهَايَةَ لَهَا ثُبُورٌ، أَوْ لِأَنَّهُمْ رُبَّمَا يَجِدُونَ بِسَبَبِ ذَلِكَ القَوْلِ نَوْعًا مِنَ الخِفَّةِ، فَإِنَّ المُعَذَّبَ إِذَا صَاحَ وَبَكَى وَجَدَ بِسَبَبِهِ نَوْعًا مِنَ الخِفَّةِ فَيُزْجَرُونَ عَنْ ذَلِكَ، وَيُخْبَرُونَ بِأَنَّ هَذَا الثُّبُورَ سَيَزْدَادُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ لِيَزْدَادَ حُزْنُهُمْ وَغَمُّهُمْ، نَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْهُ. قَالَ al-Kalbi (الكَلْبِيُّ): نَزَلَ هَذَا كُلُّهُ فِي حَقِّ أَبِي جَهْلٍ وَالكُفَّارِ الَّذِينَ ذَكَرُوا تِلْكَ الشُّبُهَاتِ.

[Page 47]

God Most High says: ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that: gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He will give you palaces.﴾ ﴿But they denied the Hour, and We have prepared a blazing Fire for those who deny the Hour.﴾ ﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they hear its raging and roaring.﴾ ﴿And when they are cast into a narrow place of it, bound together, they will cry out for destruction there.﴾ ﴿Do not cry out for one destruction today, but cry out for many destructions.﴾

Know that this is the second answer to that doubt. His words ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that﴾ mean: better than what they mentioned of worldly blessings, such as the treasure and the garden. He explained that "better" with His words ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He will give you palaces﴾. By this, He, glorified be He, draws attention to the fact that He is able to give the Messenger everything they mentioned. However, He Most High manages His servants according to what is beneficial, or according to the requirements of His will, and no one may object to Him regarding any of His actions. So He opens to one person the doors of knowledge and wisdom and closes to him the doors of worldly things, and it is the reverse for another. This is only because He does what He wills. Here there are several issues:

The first issue: Ibn Abbas said: "Better than that" means better than what they reproached you for lacking, which is the garden, because they reproached you for lacking a single garden, while He, glorified be He, is able to give you many gardens. In the narration of Ikrimah, He said: ﴿better than that﴾, meaning better than walking in the markets and seeking livelihood.

The second issue: His words ﴿if He wills﴾ mean that He, glorified be He, is able to do that, not that He Most High is in doubt, because doubt is not permissible concerning God Most High. Some people said: "If" here means "when," that is, We have already granted you gardens in the Hereafter and built palaces for you. He placed "if" only to alert the servants that one does not attain that except by His mercy, that it is contingent upon His pure will, and that no servant has any right over God, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter.

The third issue: "Qusur" is the plural of "qasr," which is an elevated dwelling. It is possible that each garden has a palace, so that it is both a dwelling and a place of recreation. It is also permissible that the palaces are plural and the gardens are plural. Mujahid said: "If He wills, He will give you gardens in the Hereafter and palaces in this world."

The fourth issue: Al-Farra' differed concerning His words ﴿and He will give﴾. Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim raised the lam (making it a nominative form, [wa-yaj'alu]), while others made it jussive. Whoever made it jussive means: if He wills, He will give you gardens and He will give you palaces. Whoever raised it means that it is a new sentence, and the meaning is: He will surely give you palaces. This is the view of al-Zajjaj. Al-Wahidi said: There is a difference in meaning between the two readings. According to the jussive reading, the meaning is: if He wills, He will give you palaces in this world, and it is not good to stop at "the rivers." According to the raised reading, it is good to stop at "the rivers" and begin anew, meaning: and He will give you palaces in the Hereafter. In the codex of Ubayy and Ibn Mas'ud it reads: "Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give."

The fifth issue: From Tawus, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "While the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was sitting, with Jibril (peace be upon him) beside him, Jibril (peace be upon him) said: This is an angel who has descended from the heavens, having asked his Lord for permission to visit you. He did not wait long before the angel came, greeted the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and said: 'God gives you the choice between being given the keys of everything that was not given to anyone before you and will not be given to anyone after you, without it diminishing for you anything of what He has stored up for you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Rather, let Him gather them all for me in the Hereafter.' Then the words ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills﴾ were revealed, to the end of the verse." And from Ibn Abbas, who said, peace be upon him: "Jibril offered me the gold of the valley of Mecca [Batha' Makkah], [page 48] and I said: 'Rather, a satisfied night and three hungry days,' and that is more for my remembrance and my request to my Lord." In the narration of Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Abd al-Wahhab, he (peace be upon him) said: "I eat my fill one day and go hungry three days; I praise You when I am satisfied, and I humble myself before You when I am hungry." And from al-Dahhak: "When the polytheists reproached the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for poverty, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) grieved over that. Then Jibril (peace be upon him) descended, consoling him, and said: 'God sends you His greetings and says: ﴿We did not send any messengers before you except that they ate food﴾ [al-Furqan: 20], to the end of the verse.'" He said: "While Jibril (peace be upon him) and the Prophet (ﷺ) were talking, a door of the gates of heaven opened that had not been opened before. Then he said: 'Rejoice, O Muhammad, this is Ridwan, keeper of the Garden. He has come to you with approval from your Lord.' So he greeted him and said: 'Your Lord gives you the choice between being a prophet-king and being a prophet-servant.' With him was a casket of light, shining. Then he said: 'These are the keys to the treasuries of this world; take them without God diminishing for you anything of what He has prepared for you in the Hereafter, not even the wing of a gnat.' The Prophet (ﷺ) looked at Jibril as one seeking counsel, and he gestured with his hand, meaning: humble yourself. So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'Rather, a prophet-servant.'" He said: After that, he (peace be upon him) never ate reclining until he departed this world.

* * *

As for God Most High's words ﴿But they denied the Hour, and We have prepared a blazing Fire for those who deny the Hour﴾, this is a third answer to that doubt. It is as if He, glorified be He, said: What they have clung to is not a doubt against you in itself; rather, what led them to deny you is their denial of the Hour, out of their reluctance to prepare for it. It is also possible that the meaning is that they deny the Hour, so they do not hope for reward or fear punishment, and they do not bear the burden of reflection and thought. Therefore they do not benefit from the proofs presented to them. Then He said: ﴿And We have prepared a blazing Fire for those who deny the Hour﴾. Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: Abu Muslim said: "And We have prepared" means: We made it ready and prepared for them. "Sa'ir" is a fierce fire of great blaze. From al-Hasan: it is one of the names of Jahannam (Hell).

The second issue: Our companions [the Ash'aris] argued that Paradise is created from His words ﴿It has been prepared for the God-fearing﴾ [Al 'Imran: 133], and that the Fire, which is the abode of punishment, is created from this verse, namely His words ﴿And We have prepared a blazing Fire for those who deny the Hour﴾. His words ﴿And We have prepared﴾ are a report of an act that occurred in the past, so the verse indicates that the abode of punishment is created. Al-Jubba'i said: "We have prepared" may mean the Fire in this world, with which God punishes the unbelievers and the wicked in their graves; and it may mean the Fire of the Hereafter, and the meaning of "We have prepared" would be: We will prepare it for them, as in His words: ﴿And the companions of the Garden will call out to the companions of the Fire﴾ [al-A'raf: 44]. Know that this objection is extremely weak, because what is meant by "sa'ir" is either the fire of this world or the fire of the Hereafter. If it is the first, then either the meaning is that He punishes them in this world with the fire of this world, or He punishes them in the Hereafter with the fire of this world. The first is false, because He did not punish them with fire in this world. The second is also false, because none of the community has said that God punishes the disbelievers in the Hereafter with the fires of this world. Therefore it is established that what is meant is the Fire of the Hereafter, and it is established that it is prepared. To interpret the verse as meaning that God will make it prepared is to abandon the apparent meaning without evidence. And since al-Hasan said that "sa'ir" is one of the names of Jahannam, His words ﴿And We have prepared a blazing Fire for those who deny the Hour﴾ are explicit that God has prepared Hell.

The third issue: Our companions argued by this verse that the one who is happy (sa'id) is the one who was made happy in his mother's womb. They said: Those for whom God has prepared the blazing Fire, and whom He reported and decreed for that, if they became believers among the people of reward, then God's judgment that they are among the people of the Fire would have become false, and His knowledge would have become ignorance. This reversal is impossible, and whatever leads to the impossible is impossible. Therefore, the transformation of those people into believers among the people of reward is impossible. It is thus established that the happy one does not become wretched, and the wretched one does not become happy.

* * *

Then, glorified and exalted be He, described the blazing Fire with attributes:

[Page 49] The first of them is His words: ﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they hear its raging and roaring.﴾ Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: "Sa'ir" is masculine, but here it appears feminine, because He said ﴿saw them﴾ and ﴿they heard for it﴾. It came feminine according to the meaning of "fire" (nar).

The second issue: The doctrine of our companions is that life is not conditional upon bodily structure. Thus the fire, in its present state, may have life, reason and speech created in it by God. For the Mu'tazilah (the rationalist school), this is not permissible. These Mu'tazilah have no proof in this matter except the extrapolation from habitual experience. Even if that were true, it would necessitate denying the breaking of habits in the case of the messengers. So their position is self-contradictory. Rather, rejecting habits befits only the principles of the philosophers. Accordingly, our companions said: God's words describing the Fire, ﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they hear its raging and roaring﴾, must be taken in their apparent sense, because there is no impossibility in the Fire being living, seeing, and enraged against the disbelievers. As for the Mu'tazilah, they had to resort to interpretation, and they mentioned several ways of doing so:

One of them: They said: "It sees them" means "it appears to them," from the expression "their houses are in view of each other" (tatarra'a), meaning they face each other. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "The fires of a believer and an unbeliever do not see each other," meaning they do not face each other, because the believer is obliged to keep away from the unbeliever and the polytheist. It is said: "The houses of so-and-so are facing," meaning they are opposite each other.

The second: The Fire, because of the intensity of its blazing and boiling, becomes as if it sees the unbelievers, seeks them out, and rages against them.

The third: Al-Jubba'i said: God mentioned the Fire but meant the guardians entrusted with punishing the people of the Fire, because seeing is possible for them but not for the Fire. It is like His words ﴿and ask the town﴾ [Yusuf: 82], meaning its people.

The third issue: One may say: Raging is an expression for intense anger, and that cannot be heard. How then did God say ﴿they heard for it raging and roaring﴾? The answer to this has several aspects:

The first: Although raging cannot be heard, what indicates it may be heard, namely a sound. It is like saying: "I saw the anger of the commander against so-and-so," when one sees what indicates it. The same is said about love. So here too: they heard for it a sound resembling the sound of one who rages. This is the view of al-Zajjaj.

The second: The meaning is: they knew of its raging and heard its roaring. This is the view of Qutrub, and it is like the words of the poet:

Girding a sword and a spear.

The third: What is meant is the raging of the guardians.

The fourth issue: Ubayd ibn Umayr said: Jahannam emits a roar such that no one remains without his limbs trembling, until Ibrahim (peace be upon him) falls on his knees saying: "Myself, myself!"

* * *

The second attribute of the Fire: God Most High's words ﴿And when they are cast into a narrow place of it, bound together, they will cry out for destruction there.﴾ Know that when God, glorified be He, described the state of the unbelievers when they are at a distance from Hell, He described their state when they are cast into it. We seek refuge in God from it with the most forceful of descriptions. Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: Regarding ﴿narrow﴾ (dayyiqan) there are two readings: with emphasis (tashdid) and without (takhfif), and the latter is the reading of Ibn Kathir.

The second issue: Several things have been related concerning the interpretation of narrowness. Qatadah said: Abdullah ibn Umar told us: "Jahannam will be so narrow for the disbeliever as the spike is narrow on the spear." The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about this and said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, they will be forced into the Fire as a peg is forced into a wall." Al-Kalbi said: The lower ones are lifted up by the flames, and the upper ones are pressed down by those who enter.

[Page 50]

فَيَزْدَحِمُونَ فِي تِلْكَ الأَبْوَابِ الضَّيِّقَةِ. قَالَ صَاحِبُ "al-Kashshaf" (الكَشّاف، تفسير الزمخشري): الكَرْبُ مَعَ الضِّيقِ، كَمَا أنَّ الرَّوْحَ مَعَ السَّعَةِ، وَلِذَلِكَ وَصَفَ اللَّهُ الجَنَّةَ بِأنَّ عَرْضَهَا السَّمَاوَاتُ وَالأَرْضُ، وَجَاءَ فِي الأَحَادِيثِ: "«إنَّ لِكُلِّ مُؤْمِنٍ مِنَ القُصُورِ وَالجِنَانِ كَذَا وَكَذَا»". وَلَقَدْ جَمَعَ اللَّهُ عَلَى أَهْلِ النَّارِ أَنْوَاعَ البَلَاءِ، حَيْثُ ضَمَّ إِلَى العَذَابِ الشَّدِيدِ الضِّيقَ.

المَسْأَلَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ: قَالُوا فِي تَفْسِيرِ قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿مُقَرَّنِينَ فِي الأَصْفَادِ﴾ [إبراهيم: ٤٩]: إنَّ أَهْلَ النَّارِ مَعَ مَا هُمْ فِيهِ مِنَ العَذَابِ الشَّدِيدِ وَالضِّيقِ الشَّدِيدِ يَكُونُونَ مُقَرَّنِينَ فِي السَّلَاسِلِ، قُرِنَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ إِلَى أَعْنَاقِهِمْ. وَقِيلَ: يُقْرَنُ مَعَ كُلِّ كَافِرٍ شَيْطَانُهُ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ، وَفِي أَرْجُلِهِمُ الأَصْفَادُ. ثُمَّ إنَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ حَكَى عَنْ أَهْلِ النَّارِ أَنَّهُمْ حِينَمَا يُشَاهِدُونَ هَذَا النَّوْعَ مِنَ العِقَابِ الشَّدِيدِ دَعَوْا ثُبُورًا، وَالثُّبُورُ: الهَلَاكُ، وَدُعَاؤُهُمْ أَنْ يَقُولُوا: وَاثُبُورَاهْ، أَيْ يَقُولُوا: يَا ثُبُورُ، هَذَا حِينُكَ وَزَمَانُكَ. وَرَوَى أَنَسٌ مَرْفُوعًا: "«أَوَّلُ مَنْ يُكْسَى حُلَّةً مِنَ النَّارِ إِبْلِيسُ، فَيَضَعُهَا عَلَى جَانِبَيْهِ وَيَسْحَبُهَا مِنْ خَلْفِهِ ذُرِّيَّتُهُ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ: يَا ثُبُورَاهْ، وَيُنَادَوْنَ: يَا ثُبُورَهُمْ حَتَّى يَرِدُوا النَّارَ»".
